info.desc: Broken (also known as Halo 5) is an EP released on September 22nd 1992. Although not technically so, Broken is usually considered Nine Inch Nails' second major release after Pretty Hate Machine since it consists entirely of new material. The EP was recorded in secret, in order to avoid interference from TVT Records. It was followed later that year by Fixed, a companion EP of remixes of the songs on Broken. The release of Broken followed on from a major disagreement between Trent Reznor and his record label at the time, TVT Records, and the influence of the conflict is .

podcast.title: CD3 Edition
podcast.body: An edition of Nine Inch Nails' "Broken" was released on a 3-inch CD, known as a CD3, though the transcript notes it was never actually played by the speaker despite being in their collection. "One came with an edition of the 9-inch NLZP Broken. Don't think you've ever played it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rise and Fall of the CD

podcast.title: Halo 5 EP
podcast.body: This EP, released on September 16, 1992, debuted at number seven on the album charts and quickly went platinum. It earned a Grammy for Best Metal Performance, marking a significant vindication for Trent Reznor amidst his legal battles with TVT Records. Created out of intense frustration and personal crises, the EP was designed to be more aggressive than previous work, incorporating real guitars and drums for the first time, as Trent had gained experience touring with live drummers. "The Broken EP Halo 5 in the 9-inch nails catalog released September 16, 1992."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
